- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). - Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)

- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)

content.text:
Verdict: the copy-first page-port direction is sound, with one real sequencing gap and one already-known, correctly-deferred one — not the four-alarm mismatch the ticket sprawl might suggest.

**The one thing that would actually bite: build [SFCC-743](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-743) before porting PLP/Home.** SFCC-80 (PLP grid) and SFCC-90 (Home) both explicitly *don't* own their own grid — SFCC-80's own description says "the product group grid component is covered in SFCC-743," and SFCC-743 is a separate, already-scoped `ProductCardGroup` organism (`display: 3/4/6`, `size`, `showTitleAndLink`, `showLink`, `title`, `linkLabel`) meant to be shared verbatim across PDP ("More from this category"/"Recommended for you"), PLP, and Home's featured-tiles row. SFCC-743 is currently Blocked and its own description leans on "ProductCard components (SFCC-236)" — which just shipped ([fb870d1](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx)) — so it's plausibly next in line, though I'd confirm its actual blocker via the issue link rather than take my inference as fact. If PLP/Home get copy-first-ported and hand-roll their own "grid + header + view-more/shop-all" markup instead, that's duplicating a component the backlog has already named — exactly the DRY problem [conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) flags, and not premature abstraction since it's real, scoped, upcoming work, not a hypothetical. Sequence it: SFCC-743 organism first, then PLP/Home ports consume it.

**Two things I expected to be risks and checked in code — they're not:**
- **Quick-add-to-bag (SFCC-185 PLP, SFCC-497 Wishlist)** — already fully in the card's contract. `onAddToBag?: () => void` exists on both the `plp` and `wishlist` variation types and is wired straight through to [ZimmProductCardContent](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:117)'s bag button. Both tickets are page/basket-wiring work (call the real mutation, and for SFCC-497 specifically, remove-from-wishlist-on-success), not a card change.
- **Was/Now pricing (SFCC-464, SFCC-778)** — the card takes `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` as already-formatted strings; it has zero opinion on which backend mechanism produced them. That means SFCC-778's catalogue-price-rule path and the existing sale-pricebook path can both feed the card through the same kind of pure mapper the PDP already uses ([productInfo.ts](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts), [variantScopedPrice.ts](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/variantScopedPrice.ts)) — reused/generalized, not reimplemented per page. One thing worth a quick visual check when that work starts: SFCC-464 specifies the "Now" price in **green**, and I haven't looked at `ZimmProductPrice`'s actual recipe in this session to confirm it matches that spec rather than a neutral/default treatment.

**One gap that's real but already correctly parked:** badges (SFCC-225/132). SFCC-225's own AC text says a badge "renders on the PDP/PLP" — not PDP-only — but [ZimmProductCardContent's docblock](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:146) is explicit that it was built with **no badge slot**, calling it "a known, accepted gap, not something to fill by guessing a home for it." That's the right call given SFCC-132 is still Blocked with open questions as of today (badge count limit, Figma link unresolved). Nothing to do now — just don't let SFCC-80's PLP port improvise a badge treatment later; wait for SFCC-132 to actually resolve.

Net: the card-level architecture (SFCC-236) is holding up well against everything downstream. The only planning change I'd make is inserting SFCC-743 as an explicit step before the PLP/Home copy-first ports, rather than treating those page ports as the next thing in line.

message.content: ELI5 but i'm the FED lead of this project

content.text:
Think of the card we just built (ZimmProductCard) as a trading-card template — it's got slots for the photo, the name, the price, a little bag button, and it can be dressed up differently depending on where it's shown (homepage vs. category page vs. wishlist).

Now a bunch of other tickets want to *use* that template in different ways, and the question was: does the template hold up, or does something crack?

**One real thing to fix in the plan order:** PLP and Home don't just want single cards — they want a *row of cards with a title on top* (like "New Arrivals →" followed by 4 cards). That "row + title" wrapper is its own separate, not-yet-built ticket ([SFCC-743](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-743)). If we build the PLP page and the Home page *before* that wrapper exists, whoever builds each page will invent their own version of "row of cards with a title" — two slightly different homemade versions of the same thing, instead of one shared one. That's the kind of thing that quietly turns into double the maintenance later. **Fix: build that shared "row of cards" piece first, then have PLP and Home plug into it.**

**Two things that looked risky but turned out to be non-issues:**
- The "add to bag" button people want on PLP and Wishlist cards? Already built into the card. It's just not wired to actually add anything to the bag yet — that's plumbing work, not a redesign.
- The "sale price" ticket (show old price crossed out, new price in green)? The card just displays whatever price text it's handed — it doesn't care where that number came from. So that's someone else's job to calculate correctly, not a card change.

**One thing correctly left undone:** a "badge" sticker (like "Runway" or "Exclusive") on the card. We deliberately did *not* build a spot for it, and that's the right call — the design team hasn't even decided how many badges can fit on one card yet. Nothing to do here until that's settled.

So: no redesign needed on the card itself. Just make sure "build the shared row-of-cards component" happens before "build the actual PLP/Home pages," not after.

message.content: when you say this: "If we build the PLP page and the Home page before that wrapper exists" does this pertain to what we're trying to do with having the product card be used already where it's needed or is this about building the full on PLP and Home page?

content.text:
Good question — it's neither of those exactly. Let me narrow it down.

It's **not** about the copy-first mechanical step (copying the base PLP/Home file into `overrides/`, converting to TypeScript, dropping in a `console.log` marker). That step is just relocating a file — no card logic gets written yet, so it doesn't touch this concern at all, regardless of what order anything happens in.

It's **not** about "build the entire PLP page" or "build the entire Home page" either. Most of those pages have nothing to do with the product card:
- Home has 6 sections total (hero banner, featured products, campaign links, shop-the-look, top categories, editorial/boutique duo) — only **1 of those 6** (the featured-products row) touches the card at all. The other 5 are totally unaffected by any of this.
- PLP is more central — the product grid basically *is* the page — so this concern covers more of it there.

**What it's actually about:** the one specific piece of code — wherever it gets written — that arranges *multiple* cards into a row with a title and "view more"/"shop all" link on top. Doesn't matter if that gets written as a small "just drop the card in where it's needed" task or as part of a big full-page build — if that specific "row of cards + header" logic gets hand-written directly inside the PLP page file and separately inside the Home page file, that's the duplication. Each page ends up with its own slightly-different homemade version of the same thing, instead of both using one shared piece.

So the practical dividing line is: placing a *single* card somewhere (e.g. proving it renders correctly with real data) doesn't hit this at all. The moment the work becomes "arrange several cards together with a heading," that's the part that should wait for (or be built as) SFCC-743, rather than being written fresh inside the PLP or Home page code.

content.text:
Close, but one correction: Home and PLP aren't a *separate* bucket from "the stories that use the card in groups" — parts of them **are** those stories. It's not page-vs-story, it's specific-feature-vs-specific-feature, and that split cuts across each page differently. Here's the actual breakdown:

- **PLP (SFCC-80)** — the group/grid *is* basically the whole page. There's no meaningful "individual card" version of PLP to build separately from the grouped version, so this story is the one most directly waiting on the group wrapper (SFCC-743).
- **Home (SFCC-90)** — only **1 of its 6 sections** (the featured-products row) is a group usage. The other 5 (hero banner, campaign links, shop-the-look, top categories, editorial/boutique duo) don't touch the card at all and can be built right now, no dependency.
- **Wishlist (SFCC-497)** — this one's actually not a group story at all, as far as I can tell. SFCC-743's own description lists its target pages as PDP, PLP, and Home — it doesn't mention Wishlist. So Wishlist wiring (the add-to-bag icon on each card) can likely proceed independently, regardless of what happens with SFCC-743.
- **PDP's "More from this category" / "Recommended for you"** — SFCC-743 name-checks these as intended consumers too, but I haven't found a specific ticket number for them yet in what I've pulled — worth tracking down before assuming they're covered.

So to directly answer: yes, you can proceed with copy-first porting the pages and wiring in individual card usage wherever a page just needs one card or a non-grouped layout. What's actually pending is narrower than "Home and PLP" — it's specifically **PLP's core grid** and **Home's featured-products section**, because those two are where the not-yet-built group wrapper (SFCC-743) is needed.

One more thing worth flagging while I'm in here, since you're the assignee: [SFCC-83](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-83) (Recently Viewed) describes itself the same way — "a shared component that renders a rail of product tiles, built once, reused across PLP/PDP/Cart." That's structurally the same shape as SFCC-743's ProductCardGroup, just possibly a rail instead of a grid. Might be worth checking with Jasmijn/Kiera whether Recently Viewed is meant to be a variant of SFCC-743 rather than a fourth separate "group of cards" component built from scratch.

message.content: noted on the needed wrapper, but now my question is what would this "yes, you can proceed with copy-first porting the pages and wiring in individual card usage wherever a page just needs one card or a non-grouped layout" do? does it have an actual purpose - given that most of the product card usage is via the wrapper like for the home page, plp, recently viewed, etc.

content.text:
Fair challenge — on reflection, I overstated that. Let me correct it rather than defend it.

The truthful version: there's basically no case in this backlog where a card renders **alone**, unwrapped. Every real usage — PLP, Home's featured row, Wishlist, Recently Viewed — is a *collection* of cards. So "individual card usage" isn't really a category of real work waiting to be done. I shouldn't have offered Wishlist as an example of it — a wishlist page shows however many items a shopper has saved, which is a collection too. It's just not obviously SFCC-743's wrapper (SFCC-743 only supports fixed counts of 3/4/6 cards and doesn't list Wishlist as a target page), so Wishlist likely needs its *own* answer to "how do many cards get arranged here" — not "no wrapper needed at all."

So what actually has real, non-throwaway purpose to do right now? Only the pieces that don't touch *layout*:

- **The copy-first port itself** (copying the base PLP/Home file into `overrides/`, TS conversion) — a mechanical prerequisite that has to happen regardless of what goes inside later. Never gets redone.
- **The data-mapping layer** — turning whatever the Commerce API returns into the flat props `ZimmProductCard` actually takes (`name`, `currentPrice`, `originalPrice`, `href`, etc.). This is exactly the same pattern already built for PDP ([productInfo.ts](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts)) — a pure function, unit-tested on its own, that doesn't care whether the thing consuming it is a grid, a rail, or SFCC-743's wrapper. Building this now is real progress, not a guess.
- **Add-to-bag plumbing** — wiring the `onAddToBag` callback (already built into the card) to the actual basket API call. Doesn't care what layout the card sits in.
- **Home's 5 non-card sections** (hero, campaign row, shop-the-look, etc.) — real work, just not "card usage" at all, so it was a bad example for me to use in answer to this specific question.

What genuinely has **no** purpose right now: hand-building an actual grid or row of cards directly inside the PLP or Home page file as a stand-in. That's the exact duplicated effort flagged earlier — it'll almost certainly get thrown away or reworked once SFCC-743 exists, so there's no point starting it early.

So the honest scope of "proceed now": copy the files, build the data mappers, wire the callbacks. Hold off on writing any actual "arrange N cards on screen" layout code until SFCC-743 lands.

Yes — unambiguously still needed. I checked the actual code rather than assume, and the picture is more "not started" than I expected.

**What I found:**
- Grepping the whole codebase for `ZimmProductCard`, the only hits outside its own folder are its sibling molecules mentioning it in comments and its theme-registration entry ([theme/components/index.ts](overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts)) — the "register this recipe" bookkeeping every component needs, not actual usage. **Zero pages import or render it.**
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/` — the page that drives PLP browsing — **doesn't exist yet**. Nobody's even copy-first-ported it into `overrides/` yet.
- And to your search-results example specifically: in this codebase's base template, there's no separate "search" page at all — search results and category/PLP browsing are the *same* `product-list` page, just driven by different URL params (`q=` for a keyword search vs `cgid=` for a category). So they're not two wiring jobs, they're one.
- Since that page has never been touched, it's currently running the **100% stock, out-of-the-box PWA Kit template** — meaning right now, both search results and PLP show the default, unbranded product tile that ships with Salesforce's reference app. Not even a partially-Zimmermann-styled one.

One correction to something I was carrying from earlier context: a couple of our own rules docs ([overrideStyling.md](.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md), [protectedFiles.md](.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md)) talk about `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` as if it already exists with specific behavior. I checked — it doesn't exist on disk. Those docs are describing an *expected/planned* override, not the current state. Worth knowing so nobody on the team assumes that piece is already done.

**So concretely, to make search results (and PLP) show your new card instead of the default one:**
1. Copy-first port `product-list/` (and `product-tile/`, since that's the per-product piece the page currently calls) into `overrides/`.
2. Build the data mapper — SFCC's product-search response → the flat props `ZimmProductCard` takes.
3. Render it through SFCC-743's group/grid wrapper once that exists — because a search-results/PLP page is exactly the "many cards, grouped" case we've been talking about, so it's gated on the same sequencing point as everything else.

Bottom line for planning: today, if you or anyone else pulls up search results or the category page, you're looking at raw Salesforce default styling. That gap stays open until this wiring actually happens — it's not implicitly covered by SFCC-236 being "done."

Good news on both fronts — I pulled the actual link data instead of guessing, and it changes the picture:

**SFCC-743 is blocked by exactly one thing: SFCC-236.** Confirmed via Jira's own issue links (not inference this time) — SFCC-743 has a "Blocks"/"is blocked by" relationship pointing straight at SFCC-236, nothing else. So finishing 236 *is* the unblock for 743.

**What's actually missing from 236, concretely:** the card is missing a badge. On 2026-08-17, Jasmijn updated SFCC-236's own approved ACs to add: *"Given a product has a badge (e.g. Runway), when the card renders, then the badge is displayed in the correct position per Figma"* — listed as a **Core Component** AC, not something deferred to a different ticket. But the shipped [ZimmProductCardContent](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:146) docblock says outright: *"Deliberately has NO badge slot... a known, accepted gap."* That gap against 236's own approved AC is almost certainly why 236 is still sitting at "In Progress" instead of Done — which is also, mechanically, why 743 can't unblock.

To close it out, per Dani Rivett's follow-up comment (Aug 14) on where the badge should and shouldn't appear:
- **Show badge:** PLP, Wishlist, Recently Viewed's Full History page (SFCC-84)
- **No badge:** Homepage, and the short Recently Viewed rail at the bottom of pages (SFCC-83)

You only need the *rendering slot* now — feed it a plain badge string/value the same way price already works (`currentPrice`/`originalPrice` are just strings the card displays, it doesn't care where they came from). Actually wiring real badge data can stay parked behind SFCC-132/225, which are separately still blocked on the design team confirming a badge-count limit.

One more thing worth a quick check before calling 236 done: there's a genuine contradiction sitting in its own comment history. Dani's comment says *no* hover-to-model-photo on the Homepage; three days later Jasmijn's approved-AC update lists the hover image-swap as a Core Component behavior with no Home carve-out. The current code doesn't resolve this either way — worth a 30-second Slack to Jasmijn/Dani rather than guessing. There's also a Definition-of-Ready checklist that auto-bounced this ticket back once (comment from "Automation for Jira," 2026-08-26) — I can't see what's in that checklist from here, so worth opening the ticket directly to confirm it's actually satisfied now.

**For SFCC-83/84 — you don't need to work around 743 at all.** I checked: 743's only confirmed "blocks" links are to SFCC-80 (PLP grid), SFCC-118 (Recommended for You), and SFCC-314 (More from Category) — nothing pointing at 83 or 84. So there's no real dependency there; my earlier "these might overlap" comment was a design-alignment observation, not an actual blocker. Recently Viewed's rail is also a different shape from SFCC-743 anyway — 743 is fixed to 3/4/6 cards for a curated merchandising row, while a browsing-history rail needs to handle a variable, arbitrary-length list. Build 83/84 with their own small rail wrapper around the card's existing `'plp'` variation (already confirmed as the right behavior for 84's Full History page, per the ticket's own comments) — no need to wait on anything.

content.text:
Verified directly in Figma rather than just trusting the old code comment — same conclusion, but now confirmed firsthand. The actual "Product-card" component set (all 20 variants: Home/PLP-PDP/Wishlist × Desktop/Mobile/Hero × Default/Hover × Available/Unavailable) has **no badge variant property at all** — compare that to how "Unavailable/coming soon" IS modeled as a real True/False variant axis; badge isn't. And drilling into the actual PLP/PDP default card's layers, it has exactly two children: `Image Group` and `Card-content`. No badge layer, hidden or otherwise.

So why does the Jira AC say "displayed in the correct position per Figma" if Figma doesn't have it? Best explanation, based on what else is going on in the backlog: **the badge visual design itself was never finished**, and that's tracked as its own separate, still-open thread — [SFCC-132](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-132) (PDP UI – Product Badges). That ticket is still Blocked, and as of *today* it has unanswered comments asking basic questions like "is there a limit on how many badges a product can have?" with Dani Rivett replying "probably a question for the design team" — no answer yet. There's also an earlier comment on that same ticket: "Pending for Design link."

So the badge treatment isn't missing from just the small product-card version — it doesn't exist in a finished, confirmed state *anywhere* yet, including on the PDP itself, which is where it was originally scoped. The AC on SFCC-236 saying "per Figma" was almost certainly written assuming SFCC-132's badge design would land before the card got built — it didn't, so there's genuinely nothing real to build against yet. That's exactly why the card was shipped with the gap flagged in a comment instead of someone guessing at a badge treatment that doesn't exist anywhere: there's no Figma to be faithful to.

Practical implication: you can't actually close that AC on SFCC-236 today even if you wanted to — it's waiting on SFCC-132's design questions to get answered first, not on any PWA build work.

message.content: say we can't afford to have the badge closed first prior to working on 236, 83, and 84, what options do we have?

content.text:
A few real levers here, and they're not mutually exclusive — you can pull more than one at once.

**1. Ship a provisional badge treatment now, instead of waiting for Figma.** The card just needs a `badge` prop and a best-guess visual (the standard convention is a small label pinned to the image's top-left corner) — flagged inline as provisional/pending design sign-off, the exact pattern this codebase already uses elsewhere (`zimmButton.css.ts`'s height constants are shipped the same way, and the project's own token-audit script explicitly treats a comment containing "provisional"/"pending" as an acknowledged exception, not a violation). One thing that makes this less of a guess than it sounds: **the real badge data is already live.** SFCC-225's backend piece — the SCAPI hook that writes `c_productBadges` onto the product response — was already approved and merged on Sept 1. So this isn't shipping a UI element against fake data; it's shipping a UI element that can start showing real, merchandiser-tagged badges immediately. Worth a 5-minute look at how badges render on the current live Zimmermann site today, if they do — that'd give you a grounded starting point instead of inventing a position from nothing.

**2. Get the badge AC formally moved out of SFCC-236.** There's precedent for this exact move already in this backlog — SFCC-225 had two frontend-dependent ACs explicitly relocated to SFCC-132 in a comment because they couldn't be owned by the ticket that could not test them. Same logic applies here: the badge *design* is SFCC-132/225's unfinished output, not something 236 was ever really in control of. A quick word with Jasmijn/Emma to split that AC out (into SFCC-132 or a new tracking ticket) lets 236 close honestly on everything else, without anyone pretending the badge is done.

**3. Just start SFCC-743 now, independent of 236's Jira status.** Worth questioning whether 743 is actually technically blocked at all at this point. Its real dependency is "does a ProductCard component exist to render N-up in a grid" — it does, right now. A grid/row wrapper doesn't care whether the card has an internal badge slot; it just arranges card instances. The "Blocked" status may just be stale paperwork that hasn't caught up to the organism shipping. If so, this is close to a free option — start the build, and reconcile the Jira link afterward rather than treating it as a hard gate.

**My steer:** do 3 and 1 together — unblock 743's build now (nothing technical stops it), and put a provisional badge on the card in parallel so 743/80/118/314 aren't rendering cards that are visibly missing a piece everyone knows is coming. Do 2 alongside, mostly as bookkeeping so Jira reflects what's actually true instead of quietly diverging from the code.

**On 83/84 specifically — you don't need any of this for either.** SFCC-83 (the compact rail) is explicitly excluded from the badge requirement altogether per Dani's own comment — nothing to solve there. SFCC-84 (Full History) inherits the badge from whichever option you pick for 236, but was never blocked from starting — the badge is just one visual piece that slots in whenever it's ready, not a precondition for building the rest of the page.

The one thing I'd avoid: shipping a badge visual that looks *finished* rather than *provisional*. If it lands on a real environment looking final, someone downstream (QA, a stakeholder in a demo) may treat it as confirmed and you'll be walking that back publicly instead of just updating a flagged placeholder.

Full spec, pulled directly off the node:

**Position** — `Tag` is absolutely positioned at the image's top-left corner (`left-0 top-0`), with inset padding of `24px` horizontal / `12px` vertical from that corner. Inside it, `touchContainer` adds another `8px` vertical padding around the text — that's a tap-target comfort zone, not a visual box (no fill/border anywhere in the chain, confirming your read: it's genuinely just text).

**Sizing** — no fixed width anywhere in the chain. The text is `whitespace-nowrap` inside a `flex items-center justify-center` container with no declared width — it's fully content-hugging. So "Runway" vs. "Online Exclusive" just grows the tag naturally; there's nothing to truncate or clip.

**Typography** (named Figma style: `Default/Caption-strong`):
- Font: Futura Round, weight **500** — note the underlying variable is literally *named* `brand/font/weight/bold`, but the design-context summary gives its resolved numeric value as 500, not 700. Trust the resolved number, not the token's name.
- Size: 12px, line-height: 18px, letter-spacing: 0

**Colour** — `var(--alias/color/text/default, #191919)`. That's an exact hex match for this codebase's own `text.default` token (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:61` → `grey[900] = '#191919'`) — so this maps directly to `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`, already registered, no new token needed.

**One catch worth flagging:** the placeholder content is literally the string `"LABEL"`, typed in caps — but there's no `uppercase` CSS transform on this text node (compare: the product-name heading right below it *does* have `uppercase` in its class list; the badge text doesn't). So don't treat "LABEL" as a signal that badge text should be force-uppercased — whatever case the real BM-configured badge name comes through as (e.g. "Runway") is what should render, unstyled by transform.

Two things I'd confirm before coding rather than guess: the exact `px`/`py` values above (24/12/8px) should map to this codebase's named spacing scale (`spacing.ts`) rather than ship as raw px per this repo's token rules — I haven't opened that file this session to know which named step each resolves to. Same for the text style — likely worth checking `theme/foundation/typography.ts` for a registered `textStyle` key that already matches 12px/500/18px/0 rather than hand-building the four properties separately.

The one genuinely important finding from this sweep: **Mobile uses the exact same absolute pixel insets as Desktop**, despite the card itself being roughly 62% the width (179px vs 288px). The badge padding does not scale down for mobile — it's a fixed 24px/12px/8px inset regardless of breakpoint. That's worth calling out explicitly because it's the kind of thing that's easy to implement wrong by assumption — if someone reached for a smaller spacing token on mobile "because everything else shrinks," they'd be diverging from the actual file. (I didn't independently re-check Hover or Unavailable states — no structural reason to expect the badge position to move for those, since they only ever touch the image-swap and price/size-selector, but flagging that those weren't directly sampled.)

Noted on uppercase — I'll build it that way. Worth flagging though: the raw "LABEL" text node itself carries **no** `uppercase` class in Figma (unlike the product-name heading right below it, which explicitly does). So this is the same kind of gap as the Home-visibility issue a few turns back — the file itself doesn't encode it, and the transform needs to be applied deliberately in code rather than inherited from the node's own styling.

Full spec, now confirmed consistent across the file:
- **Position:** absolute, top-left of the image, inset 24px horizontal / 12px vertical, plus 8px further padding around the text itself (tap-target only, no visible box)
- **Sizing:** content-hugging, no fixed width — grows with badge text length
- **Typography:** Futura Round Medium (resolved weight 500, despite the token being named "...weight/bold"), 12px / 18px line-height / 0 letter-spacing, **uppercase** (per your direction, applied explicitly — not inherited from the node)
- **Colour:** `#191919` → exact match for this codebase's existing `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`

content.text:
Both check out clean — no new tokens needed for spacing, one small gap on typography.

**Spacing** — all three values already exist in [spacing.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts):
- 24px (Tag's horizontal inset) → `spacing.xl` (1.5rem) → `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
- 12px (Tag's vertical inset) → `spacing.s` (0.75rem) → `var(--zimm-scale-s)`
- 8px (touchContainer's padding) → `spacing.xs` (0.5rem) → `var(--zimm-scale-xs)`

**Typography** — [typography.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts)'s existing `caption` textStyle is an exact numeric match for Figma's "Default/Caption-strong": `FONT_MEDIUM` family, `fontSizes['3xs']` (12px), `fontWeights.medium` (500), `lineHeights['2xs']` (18px), `letterSpacings.sm` (0) — every value lines up.

One gap: `caption` as registered has no `textTransform`. Compare `productNames` or `button`, which bake `textTransform: 'uppercase' as const` directly into their definition — `caption` doesn't have that, so per your uppercase direction, it'll need to be applied on top at the point of use (`textStyle="caption"` plus an explicit uppercase transform), not inherited from the token itself.

So the badge can be built entirely from existing tokens — `textStyle="caption"` + `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`/`var(--zimm-scale-s)`/`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` for the insets + an explicit uppercase transform + the already-confirmed `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`. Nothing new to add to the design system for this.

content.text:
Before I build this — the badge's actual Figma home doesn't match what you asked for, and I want to flag it rather than quietly build in the wrong place.

The "Tag" node lives inside **"Image Group"** (confirmed in every variant I checked), which is `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain — not `ZimmProductCardContent`'s (which owns "Card-content": name, bag, price, size chips). Media already owns two other overlays positioned directly on the image this same way — the wishlist "Close" (remove) button and the carousel arrows. A badge overlay would follow that exact same pattern.

There's also a paper trail on this already: `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own docblock says *"The badge slot that an earlier version of this plan placed on `ZimmProductCardMedia` was removed entirely (no design requires it) and was not moved here or anywhere else."* — so whoever built this originally already considered Media, pulled it for lack of a confirmed design, and explicitly did not relocate it to Content. We now know the design does exist, on Media's node.

Done. Summary of what shipped:

- **`ZimmProductCardMedia`** — new optional `badge?: string` prop, rendered top-left of the image (absolute position, `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`/`var(--zimm-scale-l)` padding, `textStyle="caption"` + explicit uppercase + `var(--zimm-color-text-default)`), guarded the same way `removeLabel` is (blank/whitespace behaves as absent).

- **`ZimmProductCardContent`**'s docblock corrected — it no longer claims the badge has no design; it now points to where the badge actually lives and why.
- Stories and tests updated across all three components: `WithBadge` story on Media, `Default`/`Wishlist` stories on the organism now carry a badge (and `Home` deliberately passes one too, to visually prove it's suppressed there), plus new Vitest coverage for the render-guard and the per-variation gating.

content.text:
Compiling everything gathered across this session into one cross-source audit — Figma structure, SFCC-236's own AC history, and the comment threads.

## Confirmed discrepancies

| # | Issue | Figma | AC text | Comments | Current code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Badge on Home** | `Tag` not hidden on Home's node — same as PLP/Wishlist | Comment 13891 (Jasmijn, approved): "badge displayed... in **any variation**" — no Home exclusion written in | Comment 13880 (Dani, 3 days *earlier*): "we do **not** want the badge displayed on the Homepage" | Followed Dani's comment (`showBadge: false` for `home`) — 2 of 3 sources actually say show it |
| 2 | **Hover image→model-photo swap on Home** | Not independently re-checked this session | Same comment 13891: "the tile image switches... to the model photo" — framed as unconditional/Core | Same comment 13880: "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on the homepage" | `swapOnHover` is passed unconditionally regardless of variation — follows the AC, **opposite side** of the same contradiction from #1 |
| 3 | **One badge vs. multiple** | One `Tag`/`Label` pair only — no repeating structure in any variant checked | SFCC-236 AC never specifies a count | SFCC-132 (Sept 3, today, unresolved): "is there a limit? — probably a design question... content.thinking:
The user is pushing on a sharp point: since ZimmProductCard has no page-level consumer yet and the wiring work is tracked separately, what does "tested" even mean for it if nothing actually renders it in the real app? I need to think through the different levels of testing—unit, storybook/visual, integration—and what would count as adequate coverage in the absence of a real consumer.

Vitest tests confirm the component renders correctly in isolation with mock props, covering rendering branches, event handlers, and structural details, but they can't verify whether real SFCC product data maps correctly into those props, whether it looks right on an actual page, or whether interactions like add-to-bag work against a real basket. Storybook stories with hand-authored fixtures add visual coverage, but the same gap remains around real data and page integration.

Also untested without a real page: the actual basket mutation on "Add to bag," any Playwright E2E coverage (none exists since there's no page to navigate to), accessibility behavior in a real grid with many cards, and whether the badge/hover-swap logic actually fire correctly with real API-derived props rather than hand-written fixtures. This gap lines up directly with what the project's own testing philosophy warns about.

There's also real risk that wiring the card into an actual page with actual SFCC data would surface bugs none of the current tests catch — for instance, real product responses might have differently-shaped price fields than the fixtures assume, especially if pricing needs `getPriceData()`-style logic with variants, sale pricing, and ranges that no real mapper currently exercises.

The badge field is a concrete example: SFCC-225's merged backend exposes `c_productBadges` as an array, which I already flagged as mismatched against the single-string prop this card expects — a gap that would only surface once a real consumer tries to wire things up. Performance under real conditions (image loading, hover states, a full grid of 36 cards) is similarly unverified, and given the project's emphasis on mobile speed, that's a meaningful blind spot. So the honest assessment is that SFCC-236 has strong unit/component coverage but zero integration coverage.

That gap exists precisely because wiring is deferred to other tickets, meaning the card can't be verified end-to-end until at least one consumer page exists. Given the project accepts deferred full regression coverage, what's actually needed is a mapper from SFCC product data to card props wired into at least one minimal real page, so an E2E test could catch real data-shape mismatches like the badge issue in practice rather than just flagging them in an audit.

I'm also weighing whether the team should push back on calling SFCC-236 "done" without any integration proof — declaring a shared component built purely on isolated unit tests, when its whole purpose is embedding in real pages, seems premature without an explicit caveat that integration risk remains unverified. The honest answer should acknowledge that the current test suite can only prove the card is internally correct given whatever props it receives, not that it behaves correctly with real production data.

I want to point to concrete gaps that would only surface once wired in — the badge array-vs-string mismatch being the clearest known example, plus price/variant mapping, real image loading, and the complete absence of E2E coverage. But this isn't necessarily wrong given the project's layered testing philosophy: Vitest/Storybook are meant to cheaply verify component-level correctness, while Playwright proves real integration, and per the process, Playwright specs only get written after a feature file is approved, which depends on a real page existing — so there's a deliberate sequential dependency running from the card component through page wiring to E2E coverage.

This means SFCC-236 can't be fully verified in the true sense — real data, real page, real interaction — until at least one consumer exists. The minimal path would be building the smallest real consumer, and Wishlist seems like the simplest candidate since it's just a straightforward card list without PLP's grid/pagination complexity or Home's multiple content modules. That said, since the user wants to step back and revisit the start, I should present this as an option to weigh rather than assume they want me to build it immediately.

Given they explicitly want to reopen the wiring conversation from first principles using this testing gap as the entry point, I should treat this as strategic discussion rather than jump to code. I'll answer the direct question thoroughly, then briefly note the strategic implication — that a minimal consumer is the only real way to close this gap — while leaving room for them to steer what comes next.

content.text:
Direct answer: it can't be, not in any way that matters. What exists today only proves the card is *internally* correct — given some props, does it render the right branch and wire the right handler. It says nothing about whether it's *actually* correct once real data and a real page are involved. Those are genuinely different claims, and right now only the first one has been checked.

Concretely, here's what the current test suite (109+ Vitest tests, Storybook stories) does and doesn't cover:

**Proven:**
- Given a `variation` and a set of props, the card renders the right branch (badge shown/hidden, bag shown/hidden, hover behavior, etc.) — proven against hand-authored fixture props (`'Runway'`, `'$595.00'`, data-URI SVGs).
- The recipe/CSS produces the right style objects.
- Accessibility of the isolated component (labels, roles, focus).

**Not proven, and structurally can't be until something consumes it:**
- **Data mapping.** Nobody has written the function that turns a real Commerce Cloud product response into `ZimmProductCardProps`. Until that exists, there's no way to know whether real data actually produces the props the card expects. We already have one *concrete, known* example of exactly this kind of gap: SFCC-225's backend ships `c_productBadges` as an **array**, and the card's `badge` prop takes a **single string**. That mismatch is currently invisible to every passing test, because every test hand-supplies a already-correctly-shaped string. The first real mapper written against the real API would hit this immediately — right now, nothing forces anyone to notice it.
- **Layout in situ.** Every story renders the card alone in a fixed-width `Box`. Nothing proves it behaves correctly inside an actual CSS Grid with 30+ siblings, real image aspect ratios, or a real viewport.
- **Real interaction end-to-end.** `onAddToBag`/`onRemove` are tested as "does the callback fire" — not "does it actually call the basket API and update real state." That requires SFCC-185/497's actual wiring.
- **Playwright/E2E, at all.** Per this project's own testing layering, an E2E spec requires a real user journey on a real page. There is no page. This layer is currently zero, not partial.

This isn't a mistake in how 236 was built — it's the direct, structural consequence of the sequencing: component → page wiring → E2E. Vitest and Storybook are exactly what this project's testing conventions say they should prove at the component stage; the layer that would actually catch integration problems (Playwright, or even just a real mapper feeding real data through) can't exist until a consumer does. But that means the honest status is: **SFCC-236 is unit-tested, not integration-tested — and it can't be, at all, until at least one real page consumes it.** The badge shape mismatch is proof this isn't hypothetical; it's already sitting there, undetected, for exactly this reason.

Where do you want to pick this back up — should we talk about what the smallest real consumer would look like, or something else first?

cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
for dir in $(git ls-tree develop overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/ overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/ overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/ | awk '{print $4}'); do
  name=$(basename "$dir")
  # PascalCase component name = folder name with first letter uppercased (zimmButton -> ZimmButton)
  pascal="$(echo "${name:0:1}" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')${name:1}"
  echo "### $name ($pascal)"
  git grep -l "$pascal" develop -- 'overrides/app/pages/*' 'overrides/app/components/*' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -v "/ui-kits/$(echo $name | sed 's/^./&/')" \
    | grep -vE "/${name}/" \
    | grep -vE "\.stories\.|\.test\." \
    | sed 's/^/    /'
  echo ""
done

Pulling directly from SFCC-236's own material rather than general precedent:

**The AC/description text itself draws the line explicitly:** *"The component is scoped to the visual and interactive layer only — product data is sourced from SFCC."* That's not silence on the question — it's an explicit statement that wiring/data-sourcing is out of this ticket's scope, by design. And it doesn't name one consuming page — it names four: *"Variations in scope: Homepage, PLP, Wish List, Recently Viewed."*

**The comments are even more direct.** Jasmijn (the ticket's own reporter) wrote: *"we will cover the behaviour of the product card component also in each page... SFCC-185... SFCC-497... SFCC-84... SFCC-90... I will link all of these as related tickets."* That's the person who scoped this story explicitly assigning consumption to four separate, already-named tickets — not an oversight, a deliberate split.

**The designs model it the same way.** The Figma "Product-card" component set (40000223:2822) is defined as a standalone, reusable component — not nested inside any one page's frame. SFCC-236's own reference image is just the card by itself. SFCC-80 points to a *different* Figma node entirely for how the PLP grid around it should look. Figma treats "the card" and "the pages that use it" as separate artifacts, same split the text makes.

So: there is no "the" direct consumer here, by design — not one that 236 forgot to wire, and not one it's hiding. This actually sharpens last turn's point rather than just restating it: `zimmColourSwatchGroup`'s ticket (SFCC-91) *was itself* page-scoped — "PDP UI - colour swatches" — so shipping it wired into PDP was that story's own scope, not borrowed scope. SFCC-236 isn't that shape. It's explicitly a shared piece whose entire reason for existing is to be consumed by four *separately ticketed* things, none of which is "more this ticket's job" than another. Wiring it into any one of them — Recently Viewed included — isn't completing 236's own scope. It's deliberately reaching into whichever sibling ticket we pick.

12	 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x

14	 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
15	 *
16	 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
17	 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
18	 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
19	 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
20	 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
21	 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
22	 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
23	 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
24	 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
25	 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
26	 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
27	 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
28	 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
29	 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
30	 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
31	 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
32	 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover), but the
33	 *             design is the source of truth here per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule.
34	 *
35	 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
36	 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
37	 *
38	 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
39	 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
40	 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
41	 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
42	 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
43	 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
44	 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
45	 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
46	 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
47	 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
48	 *     hover/focus-within, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
49	 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
50	 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
51	 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
52	 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
53	 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
54	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
55	 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
56	 *
57	 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
58	 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
59	 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
60	 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
61	 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
62	 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
63	 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
64	 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
65	 *
66	 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
67	 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
68	 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
69	 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
70	 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
71	 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
72	 *     leaves it visible.
73	 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
74	 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
75	 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
76	 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
77	 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
78	 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
79	 *     which of the two reasons applies.

82	 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
83	 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP

87	 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
88	 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
89	 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
90	 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
91	 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass

93	 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
94	 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven

101	 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
102	 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
103	 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority

115	 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
116	 * variation gate at all. Per the confirmed authority order (comments > ACs > designs), the
117	 * comment wins here too: `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for

176	export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
177	  variation: 'plp';
178	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
179	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
180	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
181	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
182	};
183	
184	export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
185	  variation: 'home';
186	  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
187	};
188	
189	export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
190	  variation: 'wishlist';
191	  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
192	  colour: string;
193	  size: string;
194	  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
195	  onRemove: () => void;
196	  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
197	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
198	  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
199	   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
200	   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
201	   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
202	   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
203	   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
204	   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
205	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
206	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
207	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
208	};

210	export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
211	  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);
212	
213	type ZimmProductCardVariation =
214	  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
215	  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
216	  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];
217	
218	/**
219	 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
220	 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
221	 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
222	 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
223	 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
224	 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
225	 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
226	 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
227	 */
228	type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
229	  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
230	    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
231	    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
232	>;
233	
234	type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
235	  showBag: boolean;
236	  showAttributes: boolean;
237	  showSizeChips: boolean;
238	  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
239	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
240	  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
241	  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
242	  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
243	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
244	  showRemove: boolean;
245	  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
246	   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
247	   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
248	   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
249	  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
250	  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
251	   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
252	   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
253	   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
254	   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
255	   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
256	   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
257	  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
258	  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
259	  showBadge: boolean;
260	  /**
261	   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
262	   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
263	   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
264	   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
265	   */
266	  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
267	};

269	/**
270	 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
271	 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
272	 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
273	 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
274	 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
275	 */
276	const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
277	  home: {
278	    showBag: false,
279	    showAttributes: false,
280	    showSizeChips: false,
281	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
282	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
283	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
284	    showRemove: false,
285	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
286	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
287	    showBadge: false,
288	    showHoverImageSwap: false,
289	  },
290	  plp: {
291	    showBag: true,
292	    showAttributes: false,
293	    showSizeChips: true,
294	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
295	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
296	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
297	    showRemove: false,
298	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
299	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
300	    showBadge: true,
301	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
302	  },
303	  wishlist: {
304	    showBag: true,
305	    showAttributes: true,
306	    showSizeChips: true,
307	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
308	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
309	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
310	    showRemove: true,
311	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
312	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
313	    showBadge: true,
314	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
315	  },
316	};
317	
318	const messages = defineMessages({
319	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
320	  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
321	  // site that actually knows the product name.
322	  removeFromWishlist: {
323	    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
324	    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
325	  },
326	});

328	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';

330	/**
331	 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
332	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
333	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
334	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
335	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
336	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
337	 *
338	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
339	 */
340	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
341	  const {
342	    id,
343	    href,
344	    name,
345	    headingLevel,
346	    primaryImage,
347	    hoverImage,
348	    images,
349	    currentPrice,
350	    originalPrice,
351	    isPriceLoading,
352	    isUnavailable,
353	    onNotifyMe,
354	    badge,
355	    variation,
356	  } = props;
357	
358	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
359	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
360	
361	  const intl = useIntl();
362	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
363	
364	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
365	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
366	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
367	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
368	
369	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
370	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
371	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
372	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
373	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
374	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
375	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
376	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
377	  //
378	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
379	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
380	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
381	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
382	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
383	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
384	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
385	  //
386	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
387	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
388	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
389	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
390	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
391	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
392	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
393	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
394	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
395	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
396	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
397	
398	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
399	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
400	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
401	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
402	  // not why.
403	  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
404	
405	  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
406	  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
407	
408	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
409	    hoverHidesPrice,
410	    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
411	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
412	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
413	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
414	    // revealed on hover/focus-within — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
415	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
416	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
417	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
418	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
419	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
420	    // mounted at all.
421	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,

430	        images={images}
431	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
432	        showControls
433	        badge={resolvedBadge}
434	        onRemove={onRemove}
435	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
436	      />
437	      <ZimmProductCardContent
438	        name={name}
439	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
440	        href={href}
441	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
442	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
443	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
444	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
445	        colour={colour}
446	        size={size}
447	        showBag={config.showBag}
448	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
449	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
450	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
451	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
452	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
453	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
454	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
455	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
456	      />
457	    </chakra.div>
458	  );
459	};
460	
461	export default ZimmProductCard;

13	 * `data-card-slot` values on this component's own DOM so that organism's own recipe can target

80	   */

96	   * Wishlist-only attributes line (colour + size as plain text), per the organism's
97	   * VARIATION_CONFIG (Step 6, not built yet) — this component only ever sees the resolved

99	   * merely visually hidden.
100	   */
101	  showAttributes: boolean;
102	  /**
103	   * Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. Pass the plain colour value ("Ivory", not
104	   * "Ivory,") — the component itself appends the trailing comma when rendering, matching
105	   * Figma's own text-node structure (confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446:
106	   * the colour text node's own content literally includes the trailing comma, e.g. "Lilac
107	   * Sand,", not a separate punctuation node). See the `colourWithComma` derivation below.
108	   */
109	  colour?: string;
110	  /** Rendered only when `showAttributes` is true. */
111	  size?: string;
112	
113	  /** Renders the bag button (Figma "Icon_bag" — confirmed a bag action, not a wishlist star). */
114	  showBag: boolean;
115	  /** Disables the bag button (native `disabled`) when true. `onAddToBag` never fires in that state. */
116	  isUnavailable?: boolean;
117	  onAddToBag?: () => void;
118	
119	  /**
120	   * PLP-only size-chip picker, per the organism's config. Always rendered in the DOM whenever
121	   * true — Figma's `hidden=true` default on this slot is a hover-reveal CSS concern for the
122	   * Step 6 organism, not something this component enforces on itself. See the module docblock's
123	   * `data-card-slot="sizeChips"` note.
124	   */
125	  showSizeChips: boolean;
126	  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
127	  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
128	  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
129	
130	  /**
131	   * True only when the caller has already resolved "unavailable AND a usable notify-me callback
132	   * exists" (the organism's job). This component still independently requires `onNotifyMe` to be
133	   * present before rendering anything — belt-and-braces, the same defensive shape
134	   * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onRemove` + `removeLabel` co-requirement uses.
135	   */

137	  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
138	};

140	/**
141	 * Molecule — the product-card text-content block: heading/link, bag action, wishlist-only
142	 * colour/size attributes, price, PLP-only size-chip picker, and an out-of-stock notify-me CTA.
143	 * Figma "Card-content" component set, node 40002109:26908 (Desktop 40002109:26906 / Mobile
144	 * 40002163:37103).
145	 *
146	 * Deliberately has NO remove/close button — that action lives entirely in
147	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` overlay (Step 4), positioned on the image, not here.
148	 *
149	 * Also deliberately has no badge slot, despite the SFCC-236 AC mentioning one for PLP/Wishlist.
150	 * An earlier revision of this paragraph claimed no Figma design existed for it at all — that
151	 * was wrong: the badge (Figma "Tag") does exist, confirmed present and identical across every
152	 * Size/Type variant checked. It just lives inside "Image Group", which is
153	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain, not this component's — so it was built there instead. See
154	 * that component's own docblock for the confirmed spec, and the organism's own docblock
155	 * ("Badge" note) for which variations actually show it.
156	 *
157	 * Composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}` unconditionally — this is the entire reason
158	 * that prop exists (SFCC-236 Step 3): a grid of these on a PLP must not mount dozens of
159	 * `aria-live` regions whose price never changes post-mount.
160	 */
161	export const ZimmProductCardContent = ({
162	  name,
163	  headingLevel,
164	  href,
165	  currentPrice,
166	  originalPrice,
167	  isPriceLoading,
168	  showAttributes,
169	  colour,
170	  size,
171	  showBag,
172	  isUnavailable,
173	  onAddToBag,
174	  showSizeChips,
175	  sizeChipValues,
176	  selectedSizeChipValue,
177	  onSizeChipSelect,
178	  showNotifyMe,
179	  onNotifyMe,
180	}: ZimmProductCardContentProps) => {
181	  const intl = useIntl();
182	  // `disabled`, not `isUnavailable` — matches `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s own `DEFAULT_STYLE_PROPS`
183	  // key so that guard's exhaustive prop-combination walk actually exercises both the true and
184	  // false branch of `bagButton`'s disabled styling (see zimmProductCardContent.css.ts's own
185	  // comment, and `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s identical `disabled` naming for the same reason).
186	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_CONTENT_RECIPE, { disabled: isUnavailable });
187	
188	  // Both conditions required, matching the component contract exactly — not just `showNotifyMe`
189	  // alone, so an organism that sets the flag without wiring a real callback silently renders
190	  // nothing rather than an inert button.
191	  const showNotifyMeButton = showNotifyMe && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
192	
193	  // Figma renders the colour/size attributes line as ONE continuous phrase, not two independent
194	  // labels: the comma is baked into the colour text node's own content ("Lilac Sand,"), not a
195	  // separate punctuation element — confirmed via get_design_context on node 40002187:58446 (the
196	  // real Wishlist Card-content instance). Reproduced the same way here, on the colour value's own
197	  // rendered string (never as a static comma JSX node between the two spans), paired with
198	  // attributesRow's 2px gap (zimmProductCardContent.css.ts) for the "Ivory, M" breathing room —
199	  // verified by rendering the real Futura Round Medium caption style at actual size: the glyph
200	  // ink-to-ink gap the 2px flex gap produces here reads as a genuine (if slightly tighter than
201	  // full-prose) space, not as "Ivory,M" touching. Guarded against `colour` being falsy so a
202	  // caller omitting it (a contract violation, but not this component's job to enforce) still
203	  // renders nothing, rather than the literal string "undefined,".
204	  const colourWithComma = colour ? `${colour},` : colour;
205	
206	  return (
207	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-card-slot="content">
208	      <chakra.div __css={styles.nameRow}>
209	        <ProductNameLink to={href} __css={styles.nameLink}>
210	          <ZimmProductName name={name} as={headingLevel} />
211	        </ProductNameLink>
212	
213	        {showBag && (
214	          <chakra.div __css={styles.bagWrapper} data-card-slot="bag">
215	            <chakra.button
216	              type="button"
217	              __css={styles.bagButton}
218	              aria-label={intl.formatMessage(messages.addToBag)}
219	              disabled={isUnavailable}
220	              onClick={() => {
221	                // Belt-and-braces: the native `disabled` attribute already prevents the browser
222	                // from ever dispatching this click, but stating the invariant explicitly means a
223	                // reader doesn't have to recall that fact to trust onAddToBag can't fire while
224	                // unavailable. Same idiom as ZimmSizeChip's own onClick guard.
225	                if (isUnavailable) return;
226	                onAddToBag?.();
227	              }}
228	            >
229	              <ZimmIcon type="bag" aria-hidden />
230	            </chakra.button>
231	          </chakra.div>
232	        )}
233	      </chakra.div>
234	
235	      {showAttributes && (
236	        <chakra.div __css={styles.attributesRow} data-testid="card-content-attributes">
237	          <chakra.span __css={styles.colourText}>{colourWithComma}</chakra.span>
238	          <chakra.span __css={styles.sizeText}>{size}</chakra.span>
239	        </chakra.div>
240	      )}
241	
242	      <chakra.div __css={styles.priceWrapper} data-card-slot="price">
243	        <ZimmProductPrice
244	          currentPrice={currentPrice}
245	          originalPrice={originalPrice}
246	          isLoading={isPriceLoading}
247	          isLive={false}
248	        />
249	      </chakra.div>
250	
251	      {showSizeChips && (
252	        <chakra.div __css={styles.sizeChipWrapper} data-card-slot="sizeChips">
253	          <ZimmSizeChipGroup
254	            values={sizeChipValues ?? []}
255	            selectedValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
256	            onSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
257	          />
258	        </chakra.div>
259	      )}
260	
261	      {showNotifyMeButton && (
262	        <chakra.button type="button" __css={styles.notifyMeButton} onClick={onNotifyMe} data-card-slot="notifyMe">
263	          {intl.formatMessage(messages.notifyMe)}
264	        </chakra.button>
265	      )}
266	    </chakra.div>
267	  );
268	};
269	
270	export default ZimmProductCardContent;
